The U. S. Fish and Wildlife Service was represented on the task force, and made contributions to the discussion of fisheries and wild-life systems involved in the mining and its attendant population effects.
The U. S. Soil Conservation Service provided extensive information regarding soils in the region and interpretation of soils information contained in consultants' reports supplied by Westmoreland Resources.
The Environmental Protection Agency (Denver), the Bureau of Land Management (Billings) and the Bureau of Reclamation (Billings) provided informal review and consultation during the early stages of the statement preparation.
State Agencies- The Montana Department of Lands provided early input and coordination into the planning and review of the working manuscripts.
The Montana Department of Highways submitted data pertaining to future road improvement and reconstruction plans.
The Montana State Air Quality Bureau supplied air quality information and consultation on air quality standards.
Crow Tribe- In accordance with BIA policy and the wishes of the Crow Tribe of Indians, extensive input was provided by several knowledgeable members of the Tribe. Representatives of the Crow Tribal Office of Coal Research, and the Crow Tribal Minerals Committee, provided manuscripts dealing with Crow culture, socio-economic systems and impacts, and other subjects of importance to the Crow people. They also contributed significantly to overall planning for this statement, and were consulted extensively for review and rewriting of various portions.
